question.text: Multifactor models are broadly classified into three categories. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that multifactor models broadly fall into three categories: macroeconomic, fundamental, and statistical. Behavioural finance and the related anomalies are discussed as a separate topic and are not listed as one of the three multifactor-model categories. The Trap: Macroeconomic, fundamental, and statistical are each genuine categories named in the workbook, so they are not the "not one of them" answer. "Behavioural Factor Model" is the term that does not appear in the workbook's classification of multifactor models. Note: Behavioural finance is covered separately from the multifactor-model classification; it informs the discussion of anomalies rather than serving as a category of factor model.
